topic_ko: 아동의 상상과 현실 인식 — 감정의 방해
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 31번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage(8문장)를 다르게 paraphrase 한다. order/insert/irrelevant/writing 은 구조상 예외.

passage: Studies indicate that, by around the age of three, children already grasp that imaginary objects cannot come to life.
This is especially evident with everyday objects — a child knows that even if they picture a pencil inside an empty box, the box will stay empty.
However, emotion can sometimes disrupt this understanding, or at least the way it is expressed.
That is, even though a child knows monsters are not real, the thought of a monster under the bed can be enough to make the child refuse to enter the room at night.

Indeed, research shows that children have a harder time displaying their understanding of the causal relations between imagination and reality when they are asked to imagine frightening things, such as monsters.
In one study, preschool children were shown an empty box and asked to imagine a monster inside it.
All the children agreed that the box was empty.
However, when they were left alone with the box, they exhibited fear and avoidance of it.
choices: how emotion can interfere with children's grasp of imagination and reality
how children gradually lose their ability to imagine as they age
the cognitive stages through which children learn to read and write
why imaginary friends are essential to early childhood development
the role of parents in reducing children's nighttime fears
theme.explanation_ko: 세 살이면 상상과 현실을 구분하지만 무서운 대상에 대한 감정이 그 이해의 표현을 방해한다는 내용. '감정이 상상과 현실 이해를 어떻게 방해하는가'가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ②나이 들며 상상력 상실, ③읽기·쓰기 학습, ④상상 친구의 필요성, ⑤부모의 역할은 본문에 없다.

passage: By the age of three, most children clearly recognize that things they only imagine cannot turn into real objects.
We should not, however, treat this recognition as something that always holds firm, since feelings can quietly weaken it.
When a child is asked to picture something frightening, like a monster, fear can take over what the child rationally understands.
For this reason, anyone trying to judge how children reason must weigh the emotional situation rather than relying on neutral tasks alone.
A child who calmly says a box is empty may still refuse to stay beside it once a monster has been imagined inside.
What the child knows and what the child does can therefore split apart.
The behavior, not the stated belief, reveals where fear has taken control.
Adults who ignore this gap risk misreading what children actually understand.
choices: Children should be encouraged to confront their fears on their own.
Adults must consider emotional context when interpreting children's reasoning.
Imagination training should begin well before the age of three.
Frightening stories should never be told to preschool children.
Parents ought to remove every imagined threat from a child's room.
claim.explanation_ko: 아이의 사고를 평가할 때 중립적 과제만으로 판단하지 말고 감정적 맥락을 고려해야 한다는 주장. ②가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①③④⑤는 핵심 주장과 무관하거나 과도한 일반화이다.

passage: Children as young as three already understand that imagined things remain imagined and cannot act upon the real world.
Yet this understanding does not always reveal itself in the way they behave.
Once fear is involved, a child may treat an imagined threat as if it were real while still insisting that it is not.
So, under the pressure of emotion, what a child knows and how a child acts can pull in opposite directions.
A preschooler shown an empty box, for example, may agree it is empty and yet avoid it after imagining a monster inside.
The gap between knowledge and behavior widens precisely when the imagined content is frightening.
This is why neutral tasks may overstate how steadily children apply what they know.
Emotion, in short, can override reason in a young child's actions.
choices: 아이들은 세 살이 되어서야 상상과 현실을 구분하기 시작한다.
무서운 이야기는 아이의 상상력 발달을 촉진한다.
아이의 지식은 나이가 들수록 행동과 더욱 일치하게 된다.
부모의 개입만이 아이의 밤 공포를 없앨 수 있다.
감정의 압박 아래에서 아이의 지식과 행동은 어긋날 수 있다.
gist.explanation_ko: 감정(두려움)이 작용하면 아이가 '아는 것'과 '행동'이 분리될 수 있다는 것이 요지. ⑤가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①세 살에 비로소 구분 시작(본문은 이미 이해함), ②③④는 근거 없음.

passage: Three-year-olds reliably understand that imaginary objects never come to life, above all in ordinary, everyday situations.
This rational grasp, however, can be unsettled by emotion — fear most of all.
A child who firmly states that a box is empty may nonetheless refuse to remain near it after being told to imagine a monster inside.
Knowledge, it turns out, does not always prevail over feeling.
When children are asked to picture something scary, they show their understanding less consistently than with neutral content.
In experiments, preschoolers agree an empty box is empty, yet display fear once left alone with it.
Their actions, more than their words, reveal the pull of emotion.
The lesson is that a young child's certainty can dissolve the moment fear enters.
choices: When Fear Outweighs What a Child Knows
How Toddlers Learn to Count and Read
The Lasting Power of a Child's Imagination
Why Empty Boxes Fascinate Young Children
Teaching Children to Tell Stories at Bedtime
title.explanation_ko: 두려움(감정)이 아이가 아는 것을 압도한다는 내용을 압축한 ①이 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ②셈·읽기 학습, ③상상력의 지속, ④빈 상자에 대한 흥미, ⑤이야기 짓기 교육은 초점이 아니다.

passage: By the age of three, children clearly understand that imagined objects cannot become real.
Yet when they are asked to imagine a monster, a child may insist the box is empty and still refuse to stay near it.
In moments like these, what the child knows and what the child does move in opposite directions.
Even though a child knows that monsters are not real, the thought of one under the bed can make the child refuse to enter the room at night.
Research confirms that children display their understanding less consistently when the imagined content is frightening.
The child's behavior, rather than the child's words, tells the real story.
Fear, in such cases, has quietly taken the wheel.
Reason is present, but it no longer steers the child's actions.
implication.underlined: Fear, in such cases, has quietly taken the wheel
choices: the child has completely forgotten the earlier lesson
the child is deliberately pretending to be afraid
the box has genuinely become dangerous
the child no longer trusts the adult's instructions
emotion, not reason, is now driving the child's behavior
implication.explanation_ko: '두려움이 운전대를 잡았다'는 비유는 이성이 아니라 감정이 아이의 행동을 주도하게 되었음을 의미한다. ⑤가 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①망각, ②의도적 연기, ③실제 위험, ④불신은 '감정의 주도'와 다르다.

order.given: Studies indicate that, by around the age of three, children already grasp that imaginary objects cannot come to life. This is especially evident with everyday objects.

blocks.A: However, emotion can sometimes disrupt this understanding. For example, even though a child knows monsters are not real, the thought of one under the bed may make the child refuse to enter the room at night.
blocks.B: For instance, a child knows that even if they picture a pencil inside an empty box, the box itself will remain completely empty afterward.
blocks.C: Indeed, research shows that children struggle more to display this understanding when they are asked to imagine frightening things rather than neutral ones.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '일상적 사물'을 (B)가 연필 예시로 구체화, (A)에서 'However 감정의 방해'로 전환, (C)가 'Indeed'로 보강. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 Indeed는 앞선 감정 논의(A)를 강화하므로 첫 순서가 될 수 없다.

summary.summary_template: Although young children rationally __(A)__ that imagination is not reality, strong feelings can __(B)__ that understanding in their behavior.
summary.explanation_ko: 아이들은 상상이 현실이 아님을 (A)know. 강한 감정이 그 이해를 행동에서 (B)override. ③.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 감정은 때때로 이러한 이해를, 적어도 그것이 표현되는 방식을 방해할 수 있다.
writing.answer: Emotion can sometimes disrupt this understanding, or at least the way it is expressed.
writing.explanation_ko: 조동사 can + 동사원형 disrupt, 'or at least the way it is expressed'로 마무리.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 모든 아이들은 그 상자가 비어 있다는 데 동의했다.
writing.answer: All the children agreed that the box was empty.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 All the children + agreed + that절.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 괴물에 대한 생각만으로도 아이가 밤에 방에 들어가기를 거부하게 만들 수 있다.
conditions: make + 목적어 + 동사원형 형태를 사용할 것
writing.answer: The thought of a monster can be enough to make a child refuse to enter the room.
writing.explanation_ko: enough to + make + 목적어(a child) + 동사원형(refuse) 구조.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Even though a child knows that monsters are not real, the thought of a monster under the bed can disrupt the child's ___________ of imagination and reality.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 감정이 방해하는 대상은 상상과 현실에 대한 'understanding(이해)'이다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Indeed, children have a harder time displaying their understanding of the causal relations between imagination and reality when they are asked to imagine frightening things.
writing.answer: 실제로, 아이들은 무서운 것을 상상하도록 요청받을 때 상상과 현실 사이의 인과 관계에 대한 이해를 드러내는 데 더 어려움을 겪는다.
writing.explanation_ko: have a harder time -ing(~하는 데 더 어려움을 겪다), causal relations(인과 관계).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Children rationally (A)___________ that imagination is not reality, but strong (B)___________ can override that understanding in their behavior.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 아이들은 상상이 현실이 아님을 안다(know). (B) 강한 감정(emotion)이 그 이해를 압도한다.
